name: fuzzy-match
description: Offline fuzzy string matching and ranking, fzf-style. Given a query and a list of candidate strings (or objects plus a dotted key path to a string field), scores every candidate that contains the query as a (possibly non-contiguous) subsequence of its characters, with bonuses for word-boundary starts, camelCase humps, and consecutive-character runs, and gap penalties for skipped characters. Returns matches sorted best-first with the character positions that matched, so a caller can highlight them. Use for fuzzy filename/command/symbol filtering, not for edit-distance/typo-tolerant search (there is no substitution tolerance here — every query character must appear in order). Output is bounded: at most 50 matches by default (1000 hard cap regardless of the requested limit), and any candidate whose serialized value exceeds 200 characters has its value omitted (index-only) in the result.

query.description: The characters to fuzzy-match, in order.

candidates.description: Strings, or objects (use 'key' to name a dotted path to a string field).

limit.description: Max number of matches to return, best-first. Defaults to 50; hard-capped at 1000 regardless of what is requested.

key.description: Dotted path (e.g. 'meta.name') into each candidate object naming the string to match against. Required if candidates are objects.

value.description: The original candidate. null when valueOmitted is true (its serialized form exceeded 200 characters) — use index to look it up instead.

valueOmitted.description: true if value was too large (>200 serialized characters) to echo back and was omitted.

truncated.description: true if there were more matches than the (default 50 / max 1000) limit returned.
